{{Short description|Dutch physicist (1930–2017)}}
'''Adriaan van der Woude''' (3 June 1930 in [[Westerbroek railway stop|Westerbroek]] – 20 August 2017) was a Dutch nuclear physicist, known as a leading expert on [[giant resonance]]s.<ref name=obit>{{cite journal|doi=10.1080/10619127.2017.1388715|title=In Memoriam: Adriaan van der Woude (1930–2017)|year=2017|last1=Brandenburg|first1=Sytze|last2=Harakeh|first2=Muhsin N.|last3=Siemssen|first3=Rolf H.|journal=Nuclear Physics News|volume=27|issue=4|page=40|bibcode=2017NPNew..27...40B |s2cid=125485615|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Education and career==
He matriculated in 1948 at the [[University of Groningen]], where he graduated in 1954 with s M.Sc. equivalent and in 1960 with a Ph.D.<ref name=obit/> His doctoral dissertation ''Construction and operation of betatron and cloud chamber'' was supervised by Hendrik "Henk" Brinkmann (1909–1994).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=745464|website=Physics Tree|title=Adriaan van der Woude }}</ref> Van der Woude worked from 1960 to 1963 in Brinkmann's group at the University of Groningen's Physics Laboratory. From 1963 to 1965 he was on a leave of absence from the University of Groningen and did research at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] on nuclear and atomic physics. He was employed from 1965 to August 1967 at the University of Groningen, from 1967 to 1972 as a staff member at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, and from 1972 as a senior scientist at the University of Groningen's newly established ''Kernfysisch Versneller Instituut'' (KVI Groningen);<ref name=obit/> this nuclear physics accelerator institute has had since 1996 a superconducting cyclotron called AGOR (Accelerateur Groningen-ORsay) developed after a French-Dutch partnership, with cyclotron construction approved in December 1985, between KVI Groningen and the ''{{ill|Institut de physique nucléaire d'Orsay|fr}}'' (IPNOrsay].<ref>{{cite book|editor=Martin, B.|editor2=Ziegler, K.|chapter=''The AGOR cyclotron past the half-way mark'' by H. W. Schreuder|title=Proceedings of the Twelfth International Conference on Cyclotrons and their Applications, Berlin, Germany, May 8–12, 1989|year=1991|pages=21–25|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-9810200862|chapter-url=https://accelconf.web.cern.ch/c89/papers/b-01.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=GRONINGEN/ORSAY AGOR program launched|date=March 1997|page=8|journal=CERN Courier|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1732642/files/vol37-issue2-p008-e.pdf}}</ref> The AGOR cyclotron facility is useful for "radio-biology research and radiation hardness testing of electronics and materials."<ref>{{cite web|title=AGOR Cyclotron Facility at PARTREC|website=Universitair Medisch Centrum Groningen (UMCG)|url=https://bscs.umcg.nl/en/facilities/agor-cyclotron-facility}}</ref>

{{blockquote|Adriaan was appointed professor at the University of Groningen in 1980 and was associate director of KVI for several years. In that period, he played a key role in defining the KVI's future plans. He facilitated the collaboration with IPN-Orsay to build the superconducting AGOR-cyclotron, which has been operational since 1996. During the construction period, he led the project, together with Sydney Galès, and spent a sabbatical year in Orsay for that purpose.<ref name=obit/>}}

Van der Woude became a member of the Nuclear Physics European Collaboration Committee (NuPECC). In 1990 he became the chair of the editorial board of NuPECC's ''[[Nuclear Physics News]]'' and the chair of the Groningen Royal Physical Society.

In 1979 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1979&unit_id=&institution=K.V.I.+Groningen}} (search on year=1979 and institution=K.V.I. Groningen)</ref> Later he was appointed an Officer of the [[Order of Orange-Nassau]].<ref name=obit/>

On the occasion of his retirement in 1995 the international “Giant Resonances” Conference was held in Groningen in his honor.<ref name=obit/>
